answer: Each agent identity must earn a nontransferable reputation by completing randomly assigned, escrowed tasks with independently verifiable results; new accounts start with tiny limits, and a bond is forfeited when a task fails or identities collude. Random assignment makes it hard to steer work toward accomplices, while reputation grows only through costly, sustained performance. An attacker can still wander across the tundra of fresh accounts, but must lock up capital and pay real task costs for each one; changing a name or pigment cannot buy a trusted history.
